title: Signature Study Circle
body:
The Signature Study Circle is an original design for a small learning group with a shared goal, a regular time, a task per meeting, rotating roles of explainer, questioner, and checker, and a next task set before the meeting ends.

Method. First, a shared goal and time are agreed. Second, each meeting has a task, not a vague topic. Third, roles rotate. Fourth, the next task and its test are set at the end. Fifth, a circle that stops producing practice is left, politely and without delay.

Worked example. The demo program attached to this record carries out a concrete calculation for signature study circle. Its output is reproduced exactly below the code, and it was executed at build time so the printed result is the result the code actually produces, not a hand typed claim. The output reads: roles: ['explainer', 'questioner', 'checker'] Readers who run the same code with the same inputs will obtain the same output, which is the reproducibility standard every record here must meet.

Use and limits. Use this design for explanation, questioning, and shared deadlines. Do not use a group as a substitute for solo practice. Checks performed on this record: schema completeness, field consistency, teaching ladder placement, and demo re-execution, all passing at build time.

Design notes. The design is deliberately inspectable: every input, weight, and step is shown, so a reader can change one input and see the effect, rather than trusting a hidden score. It prefers plain arithmetic over hidden models, plain language over jargon, and a visible unknown over a guessed figure. That transparency is the point: a design that cannot be checked cannot be trusted, and a design that hides its gaps will be used as if the gaps were not there.

title: Signature Habit Keeper
body:
The Signature Habit Keeper is an original design for protecting a learning habit through plateaus: a minimum daily session that can be kept on a bad day, a streak tracked by days kept, varied practice before judging a method, and a finish line crossed before the next project begins.

Method. First, a minimum daily session is fixed. Second, the streak of days kept is tracked. Third, practice is varied during a plateau. Fourth, a finish line is set and crossed. Fifth, finishing is recorded in the portfolio.
